headline: Revenue grows, restructuring costs tip NIQ into a loss
summary_short: NIQ's Q1 2026 revenue rose 11.1% y/y to $1,072.7M, but a $64.9M restructuring charge pushed operating income to a $10.2M loss (from $15.7M income a year ago); net loss attributable to NIQ narrowed 24.8% y/y to $90.1M on lower post-IPO interest expense.
summary_long: Revenue rose 11.1% y/y to $1,072.7M ($106.8M), led by Americas (+13.6%) and EMEA (+13.2%) segment growth, partly offset by a 1.0% APAC decline; organic constant-currency revenue grew 5.1%. Restructuring charges surged to $64.9M (from $4.6M) on the 2026 cost-efficiency program plus share-based compensation tied to the COO's departure, swinging operating income to a $10.2M loss from $15.7M income a year ago. Net loss attributable to NIQ narrowed 24.8% y/y to $90.1M ($0.31/share) as interest expense fell $25.0M on post-IPO debt refinancing, though EPS worsened from $(0.11) q/q. Cash fell to $362.3M from $518.8M on debt repayments and continued intangible-asset investment. This 10-Q includes no forward guidance.

drivers.explanation: Growth reflects solid expansion across the existing client base and increased service delivery, with pricing strategy contributing meaningfully; Intelligence benefited from broader coverage while Activation grew on higher volumes and scope of services.

Not disclosed as its own line; margin growth follows arithmetically from cost of revenues rising 10.3% (on expanded data engagements and higher variable spend) more slowly than revenue's 11.1% growth.

Restructuring, net jumped $60.3M on the 2026 Program's employee-separation and technology-investment costs plus $9.5M of share-based compensation tied to the COO's resignation, outweighing the revenue and cost trends.

Loss narrowed as interest expense fell $25.0M on post-IPO debt repayment and refinancing, and 2025 included one-time warrant remeasurement and debt write-off charges not repeated in 2026, partly offset by higher restructuring costs.
Tracks the net-loss narrowing, but per-share gains were diluted by a much larger weighted-average share count (295.0M vs 245.0M) following the 2025 IPO share issuance.
Follows the operating-loss narrowing on lower interest costs and no repeat of 2025's one-time charges, plus the depreciation and amortization add-back, partly offset by the restructuring spike.

Improvement was driven by a $24.3M favorable swing in non-cash-adjusted net loss and $65.7M of favorable working-capital movements, including higher accounts payable and deferred revenue, partly offset by higher trade receivables.

Decline reflects the quarter's own cash-flow statement: $63.6M used in operations, $59.2M used in investing (including $56.4M of intangible-asset additions), and $31.1M of net debt repayments in financing.

Modest step-down is consistent with the Credit Agreement's mandatory quarterly principal payments of 0.25% of original principal on the term loans; the filing does not itemize the quarter's exact repayment.
The quarter's $90.1M net loss reduced equity, partly offset by $11.5M of share-based compensation added to paid-in capital and $6.8M of other comprehensive income.
The 445.8% y/y jump is not operational: it reflects the July 2025 IPO and Reorganization, which added roughly $985M of net proceeds and recast the capital structure versus the pre-IPO Q1 2025 base.

Revenue grew 11.1% y/y but a $60.3M restructuring spike (2026 cost-cutting plus COO transition costs) tipped operating income to a loss; net loss still narrowed y/y on lower post-IPO interest expense and no repeat of 2025's one-time charges.
